steps.body: Units must touch exactly: no gaps and no overlaps. A gap leaves length uncounted; an overlap counts the same length twice.
steps.narration: Units must touch exactly: no gaps and no overlaps. A gap leaves length uncounted; an overlap counts the same length twice.

widget.prompt: Measure this rope with one-unit blocks — six of them, touching end to end.
widget.successFeedback: Six blocks touch exactly end to end, so the count of six is a true measurement.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: A child leaves small gaps between units. Will the count be too big or too small?
predict.reveal: Gaps mean fewer units are needed to reach the end, so the count comes out under the true length.

misconceptions: Reading a length from appearance or position instead of from same-size units laid end to end.

widget.prompt: A child lays 4 cubes along a stick but leaves small spaces between them. What is true of the count? Choose the key measurement idea.

options.label: The count is wrong — gaps hide length
options.feedback: Correct — every gap leaves length uncounted, so the measurement comes out too small.

options.label: The count is fine either way
options.feedback: Units must cover the object completely; uncovered stretches are simply never counted.

options.label: Gaps make the count too large
options.feedback: Gaps mean fewer units are used, so the count comes out too small rather than too large.

options.label: Only overlaps matter, not gaps
options.feedback: Both spoil a measurement: overlaps count length twice and gaps miss length entirely.

widget.prompt: Make this measurement trustworthy: cover the cord with seven touching one-unit blocks.
widget.successFeedback: Seven touching one-unit blocks cover the cord, so no length is missed or counted twice.
widget.alignFeedback: Start at the cord's first edge, not at a number farther along the ruler.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: Close every space and keep blocks from sitting on the same part of the cord.
widget.unitFeedback: Keep every block the same size so each count means the same amount of length.
